column1: # Double Metaphone keys, as Lawrence Philips' reference C++ produces them.
# One word per line: the word, a tab, then its keys separated by a comma --
# the primary first, and the alternate after it when the spelling is
# ambiguous enough to have one. A word with no Latin letters has no keys and
# Generated by compiling the reference implementation -- the 2000 C/C++ Users
# Journal algorithm, in the widely mirrored `double_metaphone.cc` -- and
# feeding it the list below, which is the words Philips' own rule comments
# name, the transliteration variant groups these lists actually publish, the
# names in spec/fixtures, and every hundredth word of the system dictionary
# for breadth. Regenerating it means compiling that source again; nothing in
# this repository produces these values, which is the point of them.
# The implementation was checked against the same reference over all 235,974
# alphabetic words of /usr/share/dict/words and agreed on every one; this
# file is the part of that check a spec can carry.
